description: Migration creates the checkouts ledger (item kind/id/quantity, holder kind (contact, user, location, asset, client)/id, client, out/in timestamps and actors, expected check-in, checkout/check-in notes, source, acceptance state/request, origin stock location), tenant-distributed, with a partial unique index allowing one open asset checkout per asset
Migration adds assets.holder_kind and assets.holder_id and backfills them from contact_name_id
Migration backfills every open and closed asset_assignments row into checkouts as contact checkouts preserving dates, actors, source and note

Migration backfills every on-loan stock unit into a checkout to its client (holder kind client) with loan_due_at as expected check-in, using the unit's asset as the item when present, otherwise one unit of its product
Checkout engine checkOut(item, holder, options) validates the item/holder pair, opens a ledger row, maintains current-holder columns and writes asset_history in one transaction
Checkout engine checkIn(checkout, options) closes the ledger row with actor, note and timestamp, clears current-holder columns, and writes asset_history
Engine refuses a second open checkout of an asset unless transfer is requested, and transfer checks in and out atomically

Engine validates holders by item ownership: client-owned items accept contact, location and client holders of the item's client only; MSP-owned items accept contact, location and client holders of any client; user holders must be active MSP users; contacts not shared mailboxes; asset holders same client with no self or cycle
Engine resolves the effective contact through asset-holder chains and keeps assets.contact_name_id equal to it for the asset and every asset held by it
Checking out to a location sets assets.location_id to that location

setAssetAssignee and all existing callers (form, bulk, REST, RMM auto-assign and mappings, bundles, client move, merge, import applier) route through the checkout engine, still writing asset_assignments for compatibility
Check-in sets the asset status to the chosen status, defaulting to the tenant's first active available-kind status, and optionally sets the return location
Engine publishes ASSET_CHECKED_OUT and ASSET_CHECKED_IN after commit with item kind, holder kind/id, expected check-in, source and acceptance state
Asset checkouts and check-ins also publish ASSET_ASSIGNED / ASSET_UNASSIGNED with owner type set to the holder kind, including from the Identity tile and bulk paths
New events are registered in the event bus schema, workflow event catalog, payload schemas and builders, with designer catalog rows
Tenant asset checkout settings: default checkout period, reminder lead time, default requires-acceptance, email holders on checkout/check-in, notify effective holder, and versioned agreement text
Assets settings tab lets an admin edit the checkout settings
Asset detail holder row shows holder chip with kind icon and link, expected check-in, overdue badge and acceptance badge, with Check out / Check in actions
Check out dialog supports contact, user, location and asset holders with expected check-in (defaulted from settings), note, requires-acceptance and email-holder options
Check in dialog captures condition note, status and optional return location
Checkouts panel on the asset detail page lists ledger history for the asset
Asset list shows Held by (all holder kinds) and Due columns with filters for holder kind, overdue and acceptance state
Asset list bulk Check out and bulk Check in replace bulk Assign
Full asset form and quick-add offer a holder field for all kinds that checks out through the engine
Asset drawer, client Assets tab and contact page render the holder chip for all holder kinds
Accepting an RMM signed-in-user suggestion checks the asset out to the contact with source rmm
Overdue is derived consistently (open and expected check-in in the past) and exposed in UI and API
Editing expected check-in on an open checkout is allowed from the holder row and API and re-arms the due trigger
Date-trigger source asset.checkin_due emits once per checkout at the due date and once at the reminder lead time, deduped via date_trigger_emissions

Loaner loanOut, loanReturn and updateLoanDueDate go through the checkout engine (client required, contact optional), keep stock_units status and loan_due_at mirrored, and the Loaners screen, loaners-out report and overdue view read the ledger

Migration creates acceptance_requests, acceptance_links (hashed tokens, expiry, revocation, use count) and append-only acceptance_decisions (decision, method, signer, comment, agreement hash and version, ip, user agent)
Acceptance engine service creates a request for a subject and recipient, issues and revokes links, and records decisions idempotently
A checkout with requires-acceptance creates an acceptance request for a contact or user holder and sets acceptance_state pending
Public /accept/[token] page shows the items, agreement text and holder name, and records accept (typed name) or decline (comment)
MSP can resend an acceptance request or mark it accepted on the holder's behalf with a note
Accepting stores a receipt PDF (items, agreement, signer, time, IP) as a document on the asset and the holder
Declining keeps the checkout open with acceptance_state declined and publishes CHECKOUT_DECLINED; accepting publishes CHECKOUT_ACCEPTED
Migration seeds the Assets notification category, its subtypes, and checkout receipt, check-in receipt, acceptance request, check-in reminder and overdue email templates in every supported locale
Asset email subscriber sends checkout and check-in receipts to contact and user holders when enabled and requested
Asset email subscriber sends the acceptance request email with the signed link
Asset email subscriber sends reminder and overdue emails from asset.checkin_due emissions
In-app notification to the checking-out MSP user on decline and on overdue
Location and asset holders receive no email; effective-contact notification follows the notify-effective-holder setting
Migration creates software_licenses with seats, client, software catalog link, manufacturer, vendor, licensed-to, purchase and expiry fields, reassignable flag and acceptance default
License product keys are stored through the tenant secret provider, masked in UI and API, and revealed only with license:update
license RBAC resource with create/read/update/delete is added to default roles
Engine supports license items: seats check out to contact, user or asset holders, refusing beyond seat count; non-reassignable licenses refuse seat check-in
Licenses list and detail screens with seats used/total, expiry, seat holder table and seat check out / check in
License seats show in holder Equipment sections and on assets holding seats
Date-trigger source license.expiration fires at expiration and at the reminder lead time
REST CRUD for licenses plus seat checkout and check-in, with OpenAPI docs
Migration adds stock_locations.client_id and location type client_site so a client's spare pool is inventory stock
Migration adds product_inventory_settings.asset_role (none, accessory, consumable, component) and requestable, plus issue_out/issue_in stock movement types
Inventory UI lets an admin create client-owned stock locations and set a product's asset role
Engine supports accessory checkout of quantity N to contact, user, location or client holders, writing issue_out and returning stock with issue_in on check-in, with partial check-in by split
Engine supports consumable issue of quantity N, decrementing stock and recording a closed checkout
Engine supports component install of quantity N into an asset holder and removal back to a chosen stock location
Product checkouts use stock-movement locking and never drive on-hand negative
Client Assets tab shows stock pools by role with on-hand and checked-out counts and Check out / Issue / Install actions
Contact, MSP user and client location pages show an Equipment section listing held assets, license seats, accessories and components
Printable equipment-held sheet per contact, user and location

Client portal My equipment page lists directly and effectively held assets (including MSP-owned loaners checked out to the contact), license seats and accessories with due dates and acceptance state; client-scope users also see location- and client-held items
Client portal shows pending acceptances with Accept / Decline for the signed-in contact
Assets and products can be flagged requestable from the MSP UI
Service-request form builder gains an Equipment field type offering the requester's client's requestable assets and products with availability
Service-request answer-mapping destination Check out to requester turns a fulfilled request into a checkout with source request
Portal users with client asset scope see the client's checkout ledger read-only with commercial fields hidden
Assets > Checkouts ledger screen with filters (item kind, holder kind, client, open/overdue/closed, acceptance, date range)
Checkout ledger CSV export
REST POST /api/v1/checkouts, POST /api/v1/checkouts/{id}/checkin, PATCH /api/v1/checkouts/{id} and GET /api/v1/checkouts with OpenAPI docs
GET /api/v1/assets/{id}/assignments is served from the checkouts ledger with its existing response shape
Asset check-out and check-in require asset:update plus record-level update authorization
Mobile asset detail shows holder, due date and acceptance state
Mobile technicians can check in an asset by scanning it
CSV asset import accepts holder columns (email, username or location name) and expected check-in and checks assets out on import
Asset CSV export includes holder kind, holder name and due date
Migration spec and appliers support checkouts, licenses, client stock locations and product stock as importable entities with external identifiers
Snipe-IT connector authenticates with base URL and API token and pulls companies, locations, users, categories, manufacturers, models, status labels, suppliers and hardware with custom fields
Snipe-IT connector pulls licenses and seats, accessories, consumables, components, open checkouts and checkout activity history

Snipe-IT mapping: companies to clients, users to contacts or MSP users, locations to client locations, models/categories to asset types and manufacturer/model, status labels to statuses, suppliers to vendors, with operator confirmation in preview
Snipe-IT hardware imports as assets with serial, tag, purchase, warranty, notes and custom fields, and open checkouts import as engine checkouts preserving dates
Snipe-IT licenses, accessories, consumables and components import into licenses and client stock locations with holders mapped
Snipe-IT checkout activity history imports as closed ledger rows
Snipe-IT connector runs through migration preview/apply and is idempotent on re-run
User-facing docs for checkouts, acceptance, licenses, stock pools, portal equipment and the Snipe-IT import
Checkout to a client holder is supported and shown with a client chip on asset, list, ledger and client pages
MSP-owned assets use the tenant's own client record as client_id and can be created and checked out to MSP users or lent to any client's contact, location or client

Feature flag asset-checkout gates the changed MSP assignment surfaces, ledger screen, portal My equipment and acceptance, and the Equipment service-request field; with the flag off the existing Assign UI behaves as today
